'''Sarah Depaoli''' is an American quantitative psychologist whose research is focused on [[Bayesian statistics]] and [[structural equation modeling]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morneau |first=Dominique |date=2021-01-11 |title=The making of a Primer |url=http://protocolsmethods.springernature.com/posts/the-making-of-a-primer |access-date=2025-10-05 |website=Research Communities by Springer Nature |language=en}}</ref> She is a professor of Psychological Sciences at the [[University of California, Merced]], and serves as a visiting distinguished professor at the [[University of Tübingen]]'s Methods Center in Germany.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Depaoli, Sarah, Prof. {{!}} University of Tübingen |url=https://uni-tuebingen.de/pt/fakultaeten/wirtschafts-und-sozialwissenschaftliche-fakultaet/faecher/fachbereich-sozialwissenschaften/methodenzentrum/institut/personal/depaoli-sarah-prof/ |access-date=2025-10-05 |website=uni-tuebingen.de}}</ref>

== Recognition and honors ==
In 2015, Depaoli received the Rising Star (Early Career) Award from the [[Association for Psychological Science]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Named 'Rising Star' in Quantitative Psychology {{!}} University of California, Merced |url=https://www.ucmerced.edu/news/2016/professor-named-%E2%80%98rising-star%E2%80%99-quantitative-psychology |access-date=2025-10-05 |website=www.ucmerced.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Association for Psychological Science: APS Rising Stars |url=https://www.psychologicalscience.org/rising-stars/stars.cfm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161118102121/https://www.psychologicalscience.org/rising-stars/stars.cfm |archive-date=2016-11-18 |access-date=2025-10-05 |website=www.psychologicalscience.org}}</ref>

In 2016, she was elected as a member of the [[Society of Multivariate Experimental Psychology]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Sarah Depaoli – smep |url=https://smep.org/extended-profile/dr-sarah-depaoli |access-date=2025-10-05 |website=smep.org}}</ref>
